newsitem.title: UK: Britain urges more effort to settle Cyprus problem.
newsitem.headline: Britain urges more effort to settle Cyprus problem.

text.p: Britain urged the international community on Monday to do more to end the stalemate in Cyprus and said the inhabitants of the divided island should help by softening their hardline positions.
"We are all determined that the parties should continue to be brought together and a solution should be sought for this difficult situation," Foreign Office minister Doug Henderson told reporters.
"We are determined that the situation should not be allowed to fester. All countries must bring their best endeavours to try to help specific parts of the negotiations," he said.

Henderson made his comments after talks with United Nations mediator and special Cyprus envoy Diego Cordovez, who last week presided over a failed effort to bring the island's Greek and Turkish communities together.
The five-day session ended in disarray on Friday with Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders wrangling in public.
Cypriot Greeks and Turks have been estranged since 1963 when a government in which both took part collapsed amid violence.
Turkey invaded the northern third in 1974 after a coup in the capital Nicosia engineered by the rightist junta then ruling Greece.

Henderson, who said he hoped to visit Turkey later this year for talks on Cyprus, said the islanders should realise that the time had come for them to bury their enmity and start living together in peace.
"The world has changed a lot since the last major conflict on the island of Cyprus," he said.
"The people of Cyprus have to recognise this is a changing situation and that they need to make the changes in the same way changes have been made in other parts of the world."
Cordovez, who has accepted an invitation to visit Cyprus at an unspecified future date, said the international community should not lose heart.
"I feel that support from Britain and other governments has to continue. If we maintain consultations and adopt a coherent approach we can get out of this problem," he said.

Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash has threatened to pull out of the U.N. negotiations if talks between Cyprus and the European Union go ahead early next year. The European Union decided two years ago to open entry talks with Cyprus in 1998.
Greek Cypriot leader Glafcos Clerides has vowed to pull out of any settlement negotiations if the plans for EU accession are delayed.
